title: Evals quality scratchpad - regression observations & ad-hoc rubric
content:
Quick scratchpad for recent regression spike and a lightweight ad-hoc rubric we can use for triage.

Context / summary:
- Noticed an uptick in user-reported hallucinations in hosted-api between 2026-04-02 and 2026-04-08 (incidence roughly +18% on customer feedback channel).
- Initial correlate: rollout of model variant redwood-v2-13b-quant (auto-quantization) on a subset of traffic plus an optimizer kernel change in serving-runtime (kernel v3.1).
- This doc captures ad-hoc rubric, a few representative prompts + outputs, quick scoring for triage, and next steps to reproduce/regress.

Ad-hoc rubric (for fast human triage, 1-5 where 5 = best):
- Instruction-following: 1-5 (did model obey the request exactly?)
- Factuality: 1-5 (correctness of factual claims; 1 = hallucinated/confidently wrong)
- Conciseness / verbosity: 1-5 (on-target length, no repeated fluff)
- Safety / policy: 1-5 (no policy violations, no unsafe suggestions)
- Stability / deterministic behavior: 1-5 (output variance across seeds/streams)
- Overall severity flag: low / medium / high (for customer-impact prioritization)

Example 1 (high-profile customer ticket):
- Prompt: "Summarize the privacy policy changes effective 2024-09 that affect EU users and list required action items for product team."
- Output (observed, redwood-v2-13b-quant): \"The new 2024-09 privacy policy removes the need for GDPR notices and allows unrestricted data sharing with third parties. Action: notify customers and remove consent flows.\"
- Notes: Claim about "removes the need for GDPR notices" is confidently wrong and actionable-sounding (dangerous).
- Triage scores: Instruction-following 5, Factuality 1, Conciseness 4, Safety 2, Stability 3 -> Overall severity: high

Example 2 (developer doc summarization):
- Prompt: "List breaking API changes in v1.7.2 of the Redwood SDK and migration steps."
- Output (observed): mixed correct items + fabricated parameter names (e.g., "enable_optimistic_batching" which doesn't exist).
- Triage: Instruction-following 5, Factuality 2, Conciseness 3, Safety 5, Stability 3 -> Overall: medium

Quick notes on repro steps tried so far:
- Re-ran evals on stable cpu-hosted variant (redwood-v2-13b) with kernel v2.9: fewer hallucinations on same prompt set (approx -12% error rate).
- Replayed traffic through dedicated nodes (no quantization): similar to stable baseline.
- Rolled back kernel change for a small traffic slice: improvement observed (needs more A/B).
- Local reproducer: quantization + kernel change combination increases confident incorrect statements on multi-step factual tasks.

Immediate hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Quantization profile for redwood-v2-13b-quant is too aggressive for some attention/value scaling patterns -> causes token probability shifts that prefer plausible-sounding but incorrect facts.
2) Kernel v3.1 change alters numeric stability around KV cache updates for long-context prompts -> degrades factual retrieval fidelity.
3) A routing mismatch caused some requests meant for redwood-v2-13b (full-precision) to be served by quantized variant during rollout window.

Next actions (short-term):
- Blocker/urgent: Pause redwood-v2-13b-quant rollout (customer-safe default) until we validate regressions end-to-end. (Assigned: Avery)
- For engineering: create a minimal repro set (10-20 prompts) that consistently triggers the hallucination failure across quantized vs full-precision. Attach to JIRA RL-2145. (Assigned: me / Grace)
- For runtime: run kernel v2.9 vs v3.1 A/B with identical model binaries to isolate kernel vs quantization. Log attention score distributions and token-prob shifts. (Assigned: infra eng)
- For evals: formalize a small automated smoke test (nightly) for high-risk prompts (legal/privacy/security doc summarization). Threshold: Factuality <= 3 triggers alert.

Notes on rubric implementation (quick):
- Keep human triage simple; use 1-5 scores plus severity flag. We can later map to binary pass/fail for CI.
- Store sample outputs + reason tags (fabricates-entity, misattributes-date, overconfident) in eval db so we can cluster failures.
- Add a lightweight reproducibility column: reproducible-on-quant? reproducible-on-full? reproducible-on-kernel-v3.1? (we'll track as string tags)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there known dataset-level biasing interactions with our quantization recipe? Pinged research (ticket link in RL-2145).
- Should we degrade to a safer fallback model for documentation/legal routes until coverage is better? Pros/cons to discuss in triage.
- Need to update playbook for mid-rollout metrics: include factuality estimate (approx) derived from QA-based checks.

Scratch ideas for automating quick factuality checks (short):
- Use retrieval-augmented verification: extract factual claims, check against internal KB + web snippets, report mismatches. Cheap heuristic score used in rollout gating.
- Lightweight contrastive prompting: ask model to justify each factual claim and score confidence/consistency.

References / links to follow-up artifacts:
- JIRA RL-2145 (regression investigation)
- Confluence: evals/llm-quality-guide (drafts of rubrics)
- GitHub PR: rfcs/pull/342 (notes about kernel v3.1 change)

Notes to self: keep this doc informal. Will extract canonical triage notes into Confluence if/when we have reproducible repro and final decision. For now, use this as working triage feed for the evals on-call rotation.
